column2: Compel Sardinia-Piedmont to disarm and pay reparations to Austria.
Secure the Austrian-held Lombard territory around Milan for Sardinia-Piedmont.
France and Sardinia-Piedmont conclude their defensive agreement. Napoleon III promises support if Austria attacks Piedmont, the future of Nice and Savoy remains tied to the Italian settlement.
On 23 April 1859, Vienna demands the demobilisation of the Piedmontese army and the dismissal of its volunteers. The demand brings the Italian question to the brink of war.
Cavour rejects the Austrian demand. Piedmont maintains its preparations and relies on the defensive understanding with France.
The Second Italian War of Independence

Austrian troops cross into Piedmont on 29 April 1859. France stands with Sardinia-Piedmont. The allied cause is the liberation of Lombardy, Austria seeks Piedmontese demobilisation. The German states remain outside the Italian campaign.
